data.author: krackers
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：MiMo-V2.5及后续模型的编程能力、性价比，以及公开训练过程对行业的影响。

不同观点：
• 使用者高度认可：MiMo-V2.5能胜任多种软件工程任务，成本远低于Anthropic、DS等模型，综合ROI“高一个数量级”；适合作为编码、测试代理的主力。  
• 能力评价较为平衡：模型总体像“能力强但健忘、刚加入项目的资深工程师”，通常方案合理但需要引导，多任务和大型项目能力有限；后续版本在并行处理、设计、主动补全和实现雄心上明显提升。  
• 性能存在争议：MiMo-V2.5-Pro在DeepSWE 1.1仅得19%，低于Fable（70%）、Kimi K3（69%）和Astra（74%），说明实际体验与标准化基准可能不一致。  
• 透明度获赞：公开训练进度、RL环境分数等被认为有助于学习，也可能成为小型创业公司的竞争优势；有人质疑为何IBM、Google、OpenAI、Anthropic不效仿。  
• 开放性引发行业与地域讨论：评论者认为中国公司在透明度上反而领先欧美，并担忧开源模型会冲击美国AI公司的IPO与竞争格局。  
• 训练过程引发疑问：有人质疑训练期间运行基准是否构成数据污染、公开观测是否会影响模型；另有人关注约120万美元累计成本、每秒约5美元的资源消耗、GPU规模及MFU指标。  
• 数据构成方面，有人惊讶约三分之二训练数据为源代码，并期待下一代支持多模态。

补充讨论：评论整体呈现“实际生产体验很强、价格极低”与“基准成绩和训练细节仍需验证”的张力。

data.title: Breaking the 1.58-bit Barrier for Ternary LLMs
data.author: matt_d
data.article_summary: 文章指出，三值大语言模型中“0”权重比例较高，传统五三进制打包方式未充分利用这一分布特征。作者提出BITCOS布局，用存在位图和紧凑符号向量存储权重，可在29个模型中的26个降低存储开销，最低达1.485位/权重。针对CPU和GPU优化解包后，矩阵运算性能最高提升1.28倍，端到端推理速度在CPU和GPU上分别最高提升1.18倍和1.27倍。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕三值（ternary）LLM中零权重比例较高这一现象，讨论BITCOS自适应编码能否进一步压缩模型，以及其在存储、内存和硬件部署中的实用性。

不同观点：
• 支持者认为，实际权重中零值最高约51.5%，利用分布自适应编码可将平均约1.58 bit降至1.48 bit；这对16GB显存、边缘设备和低功耗ASIC部署很有价值。  
• 有人认为这种设计本应从一开始就采用，并指出量化感知训练后，模型可能只需约增加30%权重即可达到相近质量。  
• 部分评论质疑三值量化本身，认为PTQ场景下向量量化、trellis方法更优；也有人提出用常见向量查表（如8位编码6个三值）或算术编码进一步压缩。  
• 争议集中在可变长度编码能否直接作为内存格式使用：支持者关注文件存储与传输压缩，质疑者担心推理时仍需解码回“1.58 bit/权重”，从而削弱实际收益。  
• 另有观点认为若硬件原生支持BITCOS格式，可避免展开，真正实现更高能效。

补充讨论：评论普遍认可“1.58 bit”即log₂(3)的理论来源，认为该表述有助于理解三值编码的信息熵。

Computer Science > Artificial Intelligence

(cs)
[Submitted on 14 Sep 2026]
Title:
Breaking the 1.58-bit Barrier for Ternary LLMs
Authors:
Evangelos Georganas
,
Alexander Heinecke
,
Pradeep Dubey
View a PDF of the paper titled Breaking the 1.58-bit Barrier for Ternary LLMs, by Evangelos Georganas and 2 other authors
View PDF
HTML (experimental)
Abstract:
Ternary Large Language Models (LLM) store every weight as one of three symbols $\{-1,0,+1\}$, so the cost of a ternary model is conventionally referenced to the information-theoretic $\log_2 3 \approx 1.585$ bits per weight. The prevailing deployment format packs five ternary weights into one byte (five-trit packing), and due to the power-of-two group sizes used in practice this rounds up to $1.625$ bits per weight. This effective storage bit-width treats the three symbols $\{-1,0,+1\}$ as equiprobable. We measure the actual symbol distribution of 29 ternary LLM models and find that zeros account for up to $51.5\%$ of all weights. Motivated by this finding, we introduce BITCOS, a simple distribution-adaptive layout comprised of a dense presence bitmap plus a compacted sign vector, and costs $2 - z$ bits per weight element given a zero density $z$ in the model's weights. BITCOS stores weights more compactly than the five-trit packing in 26 of the 29 tested models, and reaches $1.485$ bits per weight on the sparsest of them. BITCOS is amenable to efficient unpacking on modern processors and GPUs, and we present optimized unpacking sequences for AVX-512, AVX2 and Intel Xe2 GPUs. Measured against production state-of-the-art ternary matrix-vector multiplication kernels, at the zero densities real-world ternary models exhibit, the realized gain with our proposed layout is up to $1.28\times$. Finally, we illustrate end-to-end LLM inference results on 5 different platforms (client and server CPUs, integrated and discrete Xe2 GPUs) where decode throughput improves by up to $1.18\times$ on CPUs and $1.27\times$ on GPUs.

data.title: Nvidia announces native GPU programming in Rust
data.author: nonmaskable
data.article_summary: 文章介绍NVIDIA CUDA Rust的两条GPU内核开发路线：面向线程级编程的SIMT框架cuda-oxide，以及由编译器管理线程映射和内存布局的Tile框架cutile-rs。两者均通过Rust编译期机制保障内存安全，并可原生编译为PTX。cuda-oxide仍处于早期阶段，依赖nightly Rust；cutile-rs支持稳定版Rust，已应用于部分推理项目。NVIDIA还计划实现与CUDA C++、Python的互操作。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：英伟达推动 Rust 编写 GPU 内核（CUDA 生态）的意义、可移植性与开发体验。

不同观点：
• 支持者认为这是降低 GPU 编程门槛、提升可靠性的正确方向；Rust、Linux 内核采用及形式化验证趋势也增强了其前景。Candle、CUDA-Oxide 等项目被视为有潜力的配套生态。  
• 反对 CUDA 绑定者认为，专有 CUDA 会造成厂商锁定和大量 `#ifdef`；更合理的方式是将内核独立编写，通过 Metal、OpenCL、D3D12 或 Triton 等方式管理。  
• 更激进的开放立场希望厂商公开完整硬件手册，包括协议、缓冲区格式、ISA 和性能特征，以便开发独立驱动；也有人认为应直接面向 GPU ISA 编译，但承认硬件组合复杂且厂商锁定更有利可图。  
• 实际使用者关注 Rust 代码能否跨 GPU 架构、是否支持 Vulkan/WGPU、WebGPU/WebAssembly，以及是否与 CUDA 深度绑定；有人询问它与 Vectorware、Slang 的差异，认为自动微分可能决定工具选择。  
• 体验层面有人期待新 API 稳定，但也指出示例中输出元素顺序不一致等设计问题；另有人批评文章风格像 Claude、缺乏英伟达以往技术文档的严谨感。

补充讨论：CUDA-Oxide 可共享主机与设备端结构体，但仍是 Linux 限定、需异步且方言尚未成熟；英伟达长期 Linux 驱动体验不佳，也削弱了部分用户的信任。

Introducing CUDA Rust: Two Tracks for Writing GPU Kernels
Sep 08, 2026
By
Sri Koundinyan
,
Melih Elibol
and
Jonathan Bentz
Like

AI-Generated Summary
cuda-oxide
provides a custom rustc codegen backend that compiles SIMT-style GPU kernels written in Rust directly to PTX using the Pliron IR framework and LLVM.
cutile-rs
enables Tile-based GPU programming in stable Rust, where the compiler manages thread mapping and memory layout through CUDA Tile IR JIT compilation.
Both projects enforce memory safety at compile time: cuda-oxide uses DisjointSlice and launch contracts to prevent aliasing, while cutile-rs uses tensor partitioning and ownership to guarantee exclusive access.
cuda-oxide requires a pinned nightly toolchain and LLVM, whereas cutile-rs runs on stable Rust 1.89+ with CUDA 13.3 and no custom LLVM.
cutile-rs is published on crates.io and already used in HuggingFace's
Grout
inference engine and mistral.rs, while cuda-oxide remains in early alpha.
NVIDIA plans to support inter-language interoperability between CUDA Rust, CUDA C++, and CUDA Python so the choice of frontend does not lock developers out of other ecosystems.
Next Steps
Run the SIMT example with
cuda-oxide
by scaffolding a project and executing cargo oxide run.
Run the Tile example with
cutile-rs
by cloning the repository and running the hello_world example.
Read the
cuda-oxide book
and
cuTile Rust documentation
for detailed guides and API references.
File issues on
cuda-oxide
or
cutile-rs
to report bugs or missing features.
Join the
cuda-oxide Discord
or GitHub Discussions on both repositories to engage with the community.
Powered by NVIDIA Nemotron. AI-generated content may summarize information incompletely. Verify important information.
Learn more
In September 2026, NVIDIA announced it is leaning into native GPU programming in Rust. CUDA C++ and CUDA Python are mature, enterprise-grade toolchains, and NVIDIA will be growing and maturing CUDA Rust into 2027 and beyond
The systems layer of AI spans inference engines, serving infrastructure, drivers, and agent runtimes, and it churns constantly as models and techniques change. More and more of it is written in Rust, which catches whole classes of bugs at compile time without giving up performance.
NVIDIA is part of that shift for the same reason. The Nova Linux driver is written in Rust.
NVIDIA Dynamo
is built on a Rust core. NVTX has Rust bindings.
The GPU kernel is the exception. You can launch kernels from Rust, but the kernel itself often has to be written in another language.
NVIDIA CUDA Rust closes that gap. GPU kernels can be written in Rust, compiled natively to PTX, rather than a wrapper around code from somewhere else.
There are two tracks to use Rust, matching the two tracks CUDA itself has.
SIMT
is the model you already write in CUDA C++ or
numba-cuda
. You indicate what one thread does, and launch thousands of them.
Tile
is a newer programming model, which is also available in
C++
and
Python
. All of these frontends let you say what one
tile
of data does, and the
Tile IR compiler
does the rest.
When you are picking one to build on, reach for Tile first. The compiler decides how tiles map onto each architecture, so your source doesn’t encode architecture-specific choices, and you drop to SIMT when you need that control or want to manage memory and threads yourself.
Which language you reach for is a separate question from which model. Use the CUDA exposure that best fits the stack you already have. The two projects below are for when that stack is Rust. We plan to support inter-language interop, so the choice does not lock you out of the others.
Below is the same kernel on each track, which performs elementwise addition over 1,024 floats. Both are complete programs, both run, and both print the same line, so you can read them side by side and see what changes.
The SIMT track: cuda-oxide
cuda-oxide
is a custom
rustc
codegen backend. It intercepts compilation, routes
#[kernel]
functions through Rust MIR, the community
Pliron
IR framework, and LLVM IR down to PTX, and hands everything else to the standard backend. The GPU dialects on top of Pliron are ours. The dialects and every transform stay in Rust until the standard LLVM backend takes over.
You will need Linux, a GPU with compute capability 8.0 or later, a CUDA toolkit (12.x or newer), clang with its libclang headers, and the pinned nightly toolchain.
cargo oxide doctor
checks all of it, including the optional system LLVM. Install
cargo-oxide
, the Cargo subcommand that drives the build:
cargo +nightly-2026-04-03 install --git https://github.com/NVlabs/cuda-oxide.git cargo-oxide
Then scaffold a project and run it. The template is a complete vector addition program:
cargo oxide new vecadd_demo
cd vecadd_demo
cargo oxide doctor
cargo oxide run
The first
cargo oxide run
builds the codegen backend, so expect it to take a while. Later runs reuse the cache.

data.title: Backups Aren't Simple
data.author: afilipovski
data.article_summary: 文章指出，数据备份远比想象中复杂。重要数据不能只存一处，也不能简单用 RAID 镜像，因为硬件故障、误删、勒索软件和数据腐化都可能破坏副本。可靠备份应采用可回溯的快照，依据恢复点目标制定频率，并通过日、周、月分层轮换，在安全性、存储成本和管理复杂度之间取得平衡。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕数据丢失风险、备份策略、恢复能力及备份系统的可靠性展开讨论。

不同观点：
• 亲历损失者强调备份必要性：雷击、云盘条款变化、SD卡故障、误删源数据等都可能导致灾难；因此采取双卡拍摄、异地备份等措施。  
• 核心不是“做备份”，而是“能否恢复”。评论者认为备份必须经过验证，并关注异地保存、版本保留、灾难恢复速度；某客户火灾后通过异地备份恢复业务，证明其价值。  
• 实用主义观点认为“有总比没有好”：先将数据复制到另一介质，再逐步完善，不必等待完美方案；但也有人指出备份本身可能因脚本误删、介质损坏而制造风险。  
• 技术方案派推荐ZFS快照及异地同步、Restic/Backrest、Proxmox Backup Server，并结合3-2-1、去重、加密和GFS版本轮换；数据库需停机复制或使用导出工具。  
• 反对过度备份者认为多数人并不重视数据，损失概率和价值不足以支持复杂方案；“两类人”说法虽有警示意义，但未必适用于所有人。  
• 另有观点希望建立通用备份/恢复标准，使分布式系统能统一保存和还原快照。

49732513.article_content:
Backups aren't simple
Aleksandar Filipovski
, 2026-09-16
See also: John Salvatier’s excellent blog,
Reality has a surprising amount of detail
I read a comment somewhere that stuck with me, that went something like this:
“There are two types of people: those who have suffered a catastrophic loss of data, and those who will.”
Trying to find the source for it for this blog, it turned out that every other sysadmin has his rehashed version of the quote, but the gist of it is the same everywhere. Data loss is something that happens more often than we’d hope, and most of us are woefully unprepared for when it hits us (which is almost always at the worst possible time).
I can confirm that I had a similar experience once. When I was little we had pulled all our family photos from our home laptops and PCs onto an external hard drive, in order to free up some space. This worked beautifully until one day my dad wanted to use the drive as storage for our TV set-top box (one of
these old things
), and was prompted to format the drive. He went ahead with it, and the disk was reformatted. The index of files was deleted, and we were stuck with a nominally empty drive.
It would be easy to blame him for screwing up, but it takes beginning a career in tech to realise that there is a series of errors that lead to this kind of mistake. Firstly, we had put all of our photos in one place and didn’t bother with backups. Secondly, most consumer-facing software usually has bold disclaimers telling you that formatting a disk means losing data (which the set-top box didn’t, terrible UI). Besides, why would you even expect a non-technical person to even have to know any of this?
Thankfully we were able to get the photos restored, and it turned out to be a cheap lesson in handling data. You never keep important things in one place only. There’s about a million things that can go wrong. Your drive could die, it could be stolen, bits could rot in cold storage (hard drives have magnetic particles which can inexplicably shift, and SSDs are made of NAND transistors which leak electricity and over time, corrupt your data).
So our first principle is to have a
backup
, i.e. a copy of your files someplace else. So far so good.
This doesn’t cover the headaches of what a plugged in drive could do. Ransomware could encrypt your files, and you could do anything from an honest mistake like deleting the wrong file; up to catastrophic mistakes like running a script that overwrites everything with zeroes.
So our backup should not be a mirror of the first drive, because we also want to be able to go back in time if we mess up. Importantly, this means that mirroring your disk with something like RAID 1 is out. We need some other method that
snapshots
things.
How often do we want to take snapshots? Maybe in our case with the photos we should have run a backup every week. If we lose 6 days and 23 hours of data, that’s fine and we can live with it. This is what’s called a
Recovery Point Objective (RPO)
in IT, and in real cases, it ranges from <30 seconds for critical financial institutions which really can’t afford to lose data, to 24 hours or more for some small enterprises (if they even have a disaster recovery strategy).
Taking snapshots means that we have an increasing burden on our storage. With an RPO of 24 hours, you will end up having 7 snapshots per week. 30 per month. 365 per year, if you really don’t go and prune your snapshots. So you need to
rotate your backups
.
Let’s say I go with the naive approach and decide to keep 14 days’ worth of snapshots. When I take a new snapshot, I delete the oldest one and I add the new one. Pretty simple, but this now forces me to have a watchful eye. Maybe I keep lots of data and can’t be bothered to check if something got corrupted in the past two weeks? But then again, I can’t just store a year’s worth of backups and they’re simply not relevant to me. What happened between day 2 and day 3 of the year has almost no significance when it’s day 364. So the granularity at which we take backups must change. The closer we are to today, the more frequent the snapshots. The further back, the less frequent the snapshots.
So maybe we rotate our daily backups every 14 days, but also take weekly backups that we rotate every 7 weeks, and monthly backups we rotate every 12 months. This should be much more efficient. But again our complexity grows. We now have something called a
GFS-rotated, snapshot-based backup
. This list of adjectives will continue growing, as we’ll see in a bit.
Maybe then you take a look at
how MPEG compresses video
, and get fascinated by how a calm scene in a movie, where the protagonist speaks but otherwise doesn’t move against a completely still background can be used for compressing video. You notice that videos are composed of frames that are mostly similar to each other, only changing with a certain movement that can be represented as a vector for a fraction of the storage. Which leads you to the v
49732513.article_summary: 文章指出，数据备份远比想象中复杂。重要数据不能只存一处，也不能简单用 RAID 镜像，因为硬件故障、误删、勒索软件和数据腐化都可能破坏副本。可靠备份应采用可回溯的快照，依据恢复点目标制定频率，并通过日、周、月分层轮换，在安全性、存储成本和管理复杂度之间取得平衡。

data.title: The engineering behind the US Strategic Petroleum Reserve
data.author: johnjwang
data.article_summary: 文章介绍美国战略石油储备的工程设计。传统地面浮顶罐占地巨大且易遭袭引发火灾；地下钢筋混凝土储罐则建设成本高，并存在泄漏和地下水污染风险。最终，美国利用得州和路易斯安那州的盐丘，通过注水溶盐形成大型地下盐穴储油。盐岩渗透性低、能封闭裂缝，且注水可将石油快速顶出，兼具安全、低成本、易维护和便于快速释放等优势。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：战略石油储备（SPR）利用盐穴储油的工程原理、运行限制、维护安全及规模估算。

不同观点：
• 工程原理派：盐岩渗透率极低、不与石油反应，并会在高压下缓慢变形、封闭裂缝，因此无需钢筋混凝土内衬；向底部注水可将浮在水上的原油顶出。  
• 运行风险派：注水越多，采出油含水量可能越高；盐分溶解、洞底变形及上部剪切力也可能削弱结构。有人据此质疑为何不用原有盐水回注，以减少侵蚀。  
• 战略局限派：储备需保留约1亿至1.5亿桶以维持压力和功能，不能完全抽空；原本为少数重大危机设计，却被用于更频繁调节，可能偏离初衷。另有人担心即使快速放油，炼油厂等下游设施遭袭也会限制供应。  
• 数据质疑派：有人指出“约4.5万英亩”占地估算与300英尺直径、1130个储罐的简单面积计算不符，认为数字可能包含间距及配套设施，或存在错误。  
• 赞赏与扩展派：许多评论称盐穴方案巧妙、科普清晰，并将其与地下天然气储存、盐矿开采及化工原料生产相联系。

补充讨论：评论还关注原油长期保存期限、洞穴尺寸与循环使用情况，以及老旧但可靠的监测和数据系统；相关报告和视频被推荐作深入阅读。

49719596.article_content:
One of the most fascinating things I’ve learned about recently is the engineering behind the US Strategic Petroleum Reserve. Here are the key requirements it’s designed to meet:
Store hundreds of millions of barrels of crude oil for long periods of time to
respond to disruptions in petroleum supplies
.
Keep the oil secure against attacks by our adversaries. This is an especially hard challenge because petroleum has this tendency to light on fire, so a huge concentration of it is especially difficult to keep safe.
Release oil quickly so it can reach the market during a supply disruption.
Keep maintenance costs low and last for decades.
The actual solution, like many great engineering solutions, is incredibly elegant and simple. But before we talk about it, let’s start with how you might go about solving this:
The naive solution: External floating roof tanks
Enbridge tank farm, Cushing, Oklahoma, April 2010. Photo:
roy.luck
,
CC BY 2.0
.
Looking at the requirements, the first thing most people would probably think to do is to just take what we do commercially for storing petroleum and scale it up.
External floating roof tanks (EFRTs)
are the common solution for storing petroleum. Most tanks are confined to about 50 feet tall and 300 feet in diameter – larger than that and you start to have engineering problems with the foundation and drainage systems. This gives a volume of $V = \pi (150 \mathrm{ft})^2(50 \mathrm{ft})$, or $3{,}532{,}500 \mathrm{ft}^3$, equivalent to about 630,000 barrels of oil.
To hold 714 million barrels of oil (the full capacity of the Strategic Petroleum Reserve), you’d need about 1,130 of these tanks. If you use the standard capacity of the largest commercial petroleum farms (e.g., in Cushing, Oklahoma), you need about 45,000 acres to store these tanks. That’s basically the size of Washington, D.C., which means you’d need to acquire a lot of land.
However, the biggest downside to using tanks is that they’re incredibly vulnerable to attack. Damage can cause spills and fires, and there’s a particular weak point at the seal between a floating roof and the tank shell.
Lightning-caused fires have been documented in the seal space of open floating-roof tanks
, so a deliberate ignition source (shrapnel, incendiary) could be particularly bad.
Putting tanks underground
Next up, one might think about putting the petroleum underground. The Navy actually did this at the
Red Hill Facility
near Pearl Harbor. Built in 1943, it housed 20 enormous steel-lined concrete tanks inside excavated volcanic rock. Each tank was about 100 feet across and 250 feet tall, making it comparable in volume to a large EFRT. Altogether, the facility housed 6 million barrels of fuel. The surrounding rock provided protection from aerial attack, which was a major reason for building the facility. But this was a substantial construction project, and thousands of workers had to excavate the tunnels, install steel liners, and pour concrete. The original construction cost was
$42.2 million (~$820M in 2026 dollars)
.
Also, groundwater protection became a major challenge. A tank released about 27,000 gallons of fuel in 2014. Separate releases in 2021 contaminated the Navy’s drinking-water system, causing the Navy to defuel and
permanently close the facility
.
There’s also the question of scale. To get to 714 million barrels, you’d need roughly 119 Red Hill-sized facilities’ worth of capacity and enough space to actually put these tanks in the ground. It would be an absolutely enormous construction project that would cost hundreds of billions of dollars (which, even for the government, is extremely expensive).
The actual solution: Salt caverns
So how did the US solve this? The crux was using salt domes at four sites in Texas and Louisiana along the Gulf of Mexico. The US created massive caverns underground in these salt domes that hold about 10 million barrels each (more than the entire Red Hill facility). The DOE currently lists 60 caverns with a combined authorized storage capacity of about
714 million barrels
.
A few properties make this work:
Cylindrical caverns are excavated using water. Engineers drill into a salt dome and inject fresh water. The salt dissolves in the water, and then pumps are used to remove the resulting brine, leaving a cavern that can be used to store petroleum.
Salt contains the oil and helps seal small fractures. The rock salt surrounding the SPR’s caverns has extremely low permeability, meaning fluids have very little ability to pass through it. It also doesn’t react with petroleum. Under enormous pressures underground, salt also slowly deforms, which helps close small fractures. The salt itself can therefore contain the oil without a steel-and-concrete tank lining the cavern.
Oil floats on water, which means pumping water into the bottom of the cavern pushes the oil out. As fresh water is pumped into the bottom of the cavern, the oil gets displaced upwards into a delivery system.
As a bonus, the locati

data.title: HarnessTax: How Much Does the Harness Matter for Coding Agents?
data.author: matt_d
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：代码智能体中，Harness（工具编排、上下文管理与执行循环）对效果、成本和稳定性的真实影响，以及如何公平比较不同Harness。

不同观点：
• **影响有限但决定可靠性**：有人认为Harness主要减少工具调用失败、错误编辑等“低级错误”，对模型总体智力提升不大；Pi虽高效，OpenCode因强制提供更多上下文，可能更稳健。  
• **Harness至关重要**：另一派强调执行循环、上下文管理、反馈机制会显著影响准确率与成本；即使模型调用次数相近，不同上下文规模和工具配置也会造成巨大差异。  
• **模型与工具需匹配**：Claude更适合原生`Edit`，GPT更适合`apply_patch`；使用模型微调过的工具格式，可能比选择“官方”Harness更重要。  
• **复杂编排更优**：有人指出不能只比较单模型Harness，还应考察并发执行、子代理、模型委派等策略；“Harness”与“Agent”概念混用也会造成分析偏差。  
• **简洁或自制方案更具性价比**：Pi、轻量包装器及自建Harness被认为可达到甚至超过Claude Code/Codex；后者可能因庞大系统提示和封闭成本而更昂贵。  
• **Harness甚至可由用户承担**：简单聊天界面也能完成复杂工作，复杂Harness并非必需。

补充讨论：争议焦点是Harness究竟主要影响可靠性、上下文成本，还是实质性准确率。评论还质疑小模型和开放模型是否同样受益、API直连与OpenRouter的缓存差异，以及闭源Harness频繁更新和推理调优使基准测试难以公平、长期复现。

data.title: Japan's book scene is moving from bookstores to libraries
data.author: herbertl
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：图书馆如何从单纯借阅场所转变为社区中心，以及商业合作带来的机遇与风险。

不同观点：
• 支持社区化：图书馆可举办乐高、作业辅导、桌游、AI会议等活动，并提供免费空间和Wi‑Fi，成为重要“第三空间”；东兰辛、湾区、台湾台东等案例显示其公共价值。
• 支持适度商业合作：咖啡馆、书店、电影院或共享办公能增加就业、服务和人流；与电影院共址的案例实际运行良好。
• 担忧商业化：图书馆应是完全公共的，若依赖Tsutaya等企业，可能使经费、馆藏选择和政策受商业压力影响；咖啡和书店也可能破坏安静、无广告的氛围。
• 对日本案例的纠正与质疑：Takeo图书馆并非Tsutaya新建，而是政府图书馆改造后引入书店和星巴克；相关报道被指有未经证实的推论。曾因安全工程削减购书预算，且运营方承认选书不当。
• 对游客化的担忧：知名图书馆吸引大量游客，可能变拥挤并出现不文明行为，需权衡地方是否真正需要这种流量。
• 其他看法：书店可反映地方文化，但收藏看不懂的实体书被批评为“书籍崇拜”；Tsutaya自身也在应对流媒体冲击。

不同观点：

• 有人质疑“AI CPU”相对GPU的优势：模型权重通常只需通过总线加载一次，需进一步说明其是否主要面向推理、训练，或强调能效。  
• “技术主权”存在争议：评论指出架构基于Arm，晶圆可能由台积电/JASM制造，富士通旧晶圆厂也已出售给UMC，因此未必是真正的日本自主芯片。  
• 市场前景看法分歧：支持者认为各国都会推动国产芯片；批评者则认为市场拥挤、难以盈利，日本更应投资晶圆制造和供应链。  
• 产品计划主要面向日本、欧洲、学术及国防市场、不包括美国，被视为地缘政治和对美科技依赖变化的信号。

补充讨论：评论建议用统一模型和“每秒生成token数”衡量AI硬件，而非只比较频率和内存带宽；也有人补充了Monaka名称来源及前代产品信息。

data.title: One Year of Sponsored Servo Development
data.author: AshleysBrain
data.article_summary: 文章回顾了Servo首个由捐款资助的兼职岗位。过去一年，Josh Bowman-Matthews提名8名维护者、审查1150个PR、提交114个适合新贡献者的议题，并完善多项文档。他还协助重构JavaScript引擎集成、修复窗口行为及大量不稳定测试，支持其他贡献者获得资助。作者感谢捐赠者，并期待继续提升Servo的贡献者体验。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕 Servo 浏览器引擎的发展、资助、技术路线、实际可用性及其在浏览器生态中的价值展开讨论。

不同观点：
• 支持者认为 Servo 值得持续投入，NLnet 已资助其大规模开发；有人祝贺项目取得阶段性成功，并欢迎非 AI 类科技新闻。  
• 有人希望出现长期赞助者，不仅提供资金，还能将 Servo 接入手机或其他产品；华为、三星被举为潜在对象，以减少对竞争对手浏览器内核的依赖。  
• 部分评论质疑项目的实际用途：Servo 目前似乎还不能作为成熟浏览器引擎使用，甚至可能永远无法达到这一目标，因此需要说明其当前应用场景。  
• 技术批评指出，Servo 使用的是 mozjs，即 SpiderMonkey 的 Rust 绑定，而 SpiderMonkey 仍以 C++ 为主；既然 JavaScript 引擎是内存漏洞的重要攻击面，仅外围采用 Rust 的安全收益可能有限。  
• 有人将 Servo 比作“Hurd 式”的浏览器引擎，暗示其长期开发、距离实用仍较遥远；另有人认为它是 Ladybird 的替代选择，但不认同 Ladybird 近期的发展方向。  
• 另有观点质疑非营利项目的成本，尤其是总部设在硅谷、支付旧金山薪资是否必要；同时批评某些项目投入巨大精力进行并行化，却仍受传统冯·诺依曼架构限制。

补充讨论：争议焦点主要在于 Servo 的投入产出比、技术路线（尤其是 JS 引擎）、距离实际商用的成熟度，以及非营利项目的资金使用效率。

49737849.article_content:
Your Donations at Work: One Year of Sponsored Servo Development
Looking back on Servo's first donation-funded role.
Posted
2026-09-15
Last September, the Servo project
announced
that long-time maintainer
Josh Bowman-Matthews (@jdm)
would work part-time on improving the Servo contributor experience, entirely funded by the monthly donations on
OpenCollective
and
GitHub
.
In his own words, here is a look back over the past year!
First of all, I am enormously grateful to everyone who financially supports Servo, as those donations have enabled me to devote significant time to a project that I care a lot about.
Some highlights from that funded work that I’m proud of:
I nominated
8 new
maintainers
I reviewed
1150 pull requests
I filed
114 issues
targeted at newer contributors (92% of them have been fixed)
I wrote
new documentation
about
borrow hazards
,
experimental features
, the
AI policy
,
finding things to do
, and fixing
stable
and
intermittent
test failures
On top of that, I spent time diagnosing unexpected failures in others’ PRs and fixed numerous intermittent test failures that made merging PRs more difficult for everyone.
A few pieces of work from this period that stand out to me:
supporting a
large scale rewrite
of Servo’s JS engine integration to address intermittent panics related to garbage collection—I reviewed lots of pull requests, but also filed many issues that enabled the work addressing the panics to be spread across many other contributors
getting tagged in to help understand test failures, uncovering our
broken window.open behaviour
, and eventually making
a lot of flaky tests
more stable
supporting another contributor’s grant proposal to work on Servo that
was approved!
This role I’ve carved out means a lot to me—I’ve found a healthy balance that allows me to spend time with my family as well as make meaningful contributions to Servo, and I get to spend a lot of time looking for ways to make the project more accessible for others.
A big thank you to everybody supporting the project and my work; each individual monthly donation makes a big difference!
I’m excited to see what’s possible in the coming year.

data.title: I had Gemini train its own replacement for $9
data.author: p-s-v
data.article_summary: 作者用 Gemini 3.1 Pro 为4290条刀具论坛评论标注品牌、型号和材质，再微调459M参数的GLiNER模型替代持续付费调用。通过字符串匹配生成偏移、加入负样本并修正训练配置，模型在225条验证集上达到0.83 F1；标注花费9美元、GPU约2.5美元，24分钟完成。但评估仅以未经人工核验的Gemini结果为标准，且多次训练失败、调试耗时数日。

不同观点：

• **质疑实际使用场景**：foltik 认为挑选刀具时，亲自到店体验比分析 Reddit 争论更有效，因为不同刀具差异有限、网络讨论信噪比不高。  
• **关注技术本质与泛化能力**：bguberfain 认为项目可能只是把刀具领域词汇映射到类别，简单词典也能完成；建议按未见过的词或品牌划分训练集与验证集，以检验 NER/分类模型能否识别新品牌。PcChip进一步追问新品牌出现后的处理方式。m00dy指出 GLiNER 的训练数据集规模较小。

49740330.article_content:
This article was written with the assistance of AI. If that bothers you, stop reading here. The numbers are real: every score comes from the ten training runs described below, and the full run log is in the linked knife.day write-up.
The knife.day write-up, with the full run log
I like to cook, and somewhere along the way that turned into an obsession with high-end chef's knives. So I scrape the Reddit threads where people argue about them and pull out every brand, model and steel they mention, to see what is getting bought and argued about.
Picking product names out of text is a job called named-entity recognition, and small models have done it for a decade. I was doing it with Gemini 3.1 Pro, one paid API call per comment. Overkill, but it worked: from "picked up a Mazaki in white #2, way better than my old Fibrox" it returned Mazaki as a brand, Fibrox as a model and white #2 as a steel, and nothing else. But the scraper pulls every new comment, so the bill grew with how much people posted, and the only way to cap it was to skip comments.
The obvious replacement, an open NER model called GLiNER run zero-shot, cut the cost to nothing and the accuracy to about 0.65 F1 against Gemini's answers. That gap is what the rest of this is about: could Gemini label 4,290 comments once and teach GLiNER to close it?
What
:
Fine-tuned GLiNER large v2.5 (459M) to tag brands, models and materials in Reddit comments, on labels Gemini 3.1 Pro wrote once.
Why
:
Zero-shot GLiNER scored about 0.65 F1 (est.). Gemini scored well and billed every comment for as long as the scraper ran.
Approach
:
Ask Gemini for strings, not offsets. Compute offsets in code. Add comments with no products in them as negatives. Lock a 225-comment validation set before the second run.
Problems
:
Five of ten runs produced no usable model. Three failed on configuration. Two failed on a tensor called words_mask that I filled the way you fill an attention mask.
Result
:
0.83 F1 against Gemini's labels after 24 minutes on a Tesla T4. $9 of labels, about $2.50 of GPU time, and days of debugging.
What I set out to do
The plan had three steps. Have Gemini label a few thousand Reddit comments once, marking every brand, model and steel. Train GLiNER on those labels. Then run GLiNER on my own machine for every comment after that, and stop calling Gemini.
Gemini labeled 4,290 comments for $9, or $0.0021 a comment. That means the trained model pays for itself at roughly comment 4,291, as long as later comments are about the same length and it runs on a GPU I already own. The test of success was simple: on 225 comments the model had never seen, how often does it tag the same words Gemini tagged? One catch to keep in mind for every score in this article. Nobody checked Gemini's labels by hand, so the model is graded against Gemini, not against the truth. Where Gemini was wrong, the model gets marked right for copying the mistake and wrong for fixing it.
The approach
Gemini labeled the comments through OpenRouter at temperature 0 in 25 minutes. The prompt decision that mattered most was to never ask the model for character offsets. It counts characters badly and returns spans off by two or three positions. The prompt asks for the exact substring and a label, and TypeScript finds the offsets. If the string is not in the comment, the entity is dropped and logged.
// The model returns strings. Code computes the offsets.
{ "entities": [
{ "text": "Benchmade", "label": "knife brand" },
{ "text": "940", "label": "knife model" },
{ "text": "S30V", "label": "knife steel" }
] }
Product names are full of punctuation a generic tokenizer splits, so a regex keeps VG-10, CPM-154 and 1.4116 whole and emits every other non-space character as its own token. Spans that still miss a token boundary are dropped rather than guessed. About 30% of the training set is comments that contain a known false-positive trigger (gyuto, carbon, handle, patina) and no product, labeled as empty. Before the second run I set aside 225 comments as a validation set and never touched them again. Training ran on a Tesla T4 on Modal with the HF Trainer.

gradient_accumulation_steps = 8
learning_rate = 1e-5
threshold = 0.45

Roughly 30% of examples deliberately contain no entities at all.
What went wrong
For five runs the model learned nothing. The first three failed on configuration, and anyone using the HF Trainer with GLiNER will hit them in an afternoon.

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕LLM的实用价值、交互体验、思想偏向及其社会影响展开讨论。

不同观点：
• 实用派认为LLM能替代付费应用、节省成本，并在互联网搜索被SEO和广告污染后，成为获取信息的现实工具；也有人建议把它当作工具，用于生成代码、维护网站，而非聊天伙伴。  
• 反感交互体验者认为LLM像“最烦人的同事”，回答模式单一、令人不适，因此将其严格限制为代码生成器；有人怀念早期模型更古怪、有趣的风格，认为RL和系统提示提升了实用性，却牺牲了个性。  
• 批评者指出，LLM的回答空间受安全规范、提示词和“无偏见”“平衡呈现”等目标限制，容易回归平均、过度纠正，难以展现观点细节，可能加剧社会群体思维。  
• 现实主义者认为，避免不喜欢或不信任的人虽合理，却是有条件的“生活窍门”，在多数职业环境中并不可行；也有人怀疑这种相处方式未来是否仍能维持。  
• 另有评论追问硅谷“brogrammer”文化与LLM产品之间的关系，质疑其是否塑造了模型的风格与局限。

补充讨论：争议焦点在于，LLM究竟应优先成为高效、可控的工具，还是保留更丰富、个性化甚至不完美的交流特征；评论整体承认其有用，但对其令人不快的互动方式和潜在同质化影响保持警惕。

data.title: Show HN: I built a new version of my fun spatial 3D online meeting app
data.author: pawelwentpawel
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了一款基于浏览器的趣味在线会议与虚拟空间平台。用户可自由移动、通过空间音频自然交流，参与游戏、破冰活动、白板协作、线上演讲和问答等。平台支持自定义地图、品牌与房间布局，适用于远程办公、在线课堂、虚拟活动、社交聚会及团队建设，无需安装即可快速创建和使用。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕一款结合视频、虚拟空间与社交互动的在线平台，评论集中于使用场景、交互体验、技术性能及产品展示方式。

不同观点：
• 反对或需求有限：有人认为线上会议应尽量缩短，远程团队并不需要通过更“休闲”的会议增强关系；若想社交，Discord和线上游戏已足够。  
• 偏向朋友社交：多位评论者认为产品更适合朋友聚会、社交或游戏，而非工作与商务场景，建议加强游戏化和社交属性。  
• 认可产品体验：有人称其处于 Gather 与 Katmai 之间，体验自然；“圆形头像叠加实时视频”比许多类似产品更舒服。也有人期待其成为类似 Habbo Hotel 的模块化虚拟会议空间。  
• 技术与可用性问题：评论指出性能不佳、频繁卡顿、首页占用近100% CPU；注册接口返回403且页面未显示验证码。  
• 展示真实性争议：有人怀疑宣传视频中的真人画面由AI生成，认为这会损害第一印象、引发“粗制滥造”的观感，建议使用真实演示或现场Demo。  
• 视角偏好：鸟瞰视角便于观察参与者互动，也适合容易被第一人称游戏弄头痛的人，但可能改变线下活动的社交动态。

补充讨论：产品被多次拿来与 Gather、WorkAdventure、Mozilla Hubs、Meta VR 等比较；整体评价偏正面，但性能、自托管、注册流程和宣传素材是主要争议与改进焦点。

data.title: CCC invites all model citizens to 40C3
data.author: antonly
data.article_summary: 混沌电脑俱乐部将于2026年12月27日至30日在汉堡展览馆举办第40届混沌通信大会（40C3），主题为“模范公民”。大会聚焦技术、社会与公民自由，倡导多元、团结和共同创造，反思威权主义趋势。现面向公众征集演讲、音乐、艺术及朋克表演等项目，邀请大家参与塑造这一志愿者驱动的黑客盛会。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕CCC大会的社区文化、包容性、参与门槛及其与DEFCON的对比展开讨论。

不同观点：
• 高度认可者认为CCC是少见的“建设型”黑客社区：大量开源项目、艺术与朋克文化、自建通信网络、志愿服务和非商业氛围，远胜充满逐利和企业色彩的DEFCON。  
• 批评者指出，CCC虽整体值得参加，但存在许多令人不适的“细小负面互动”：因佩戴巴勒斯坦头巾被指责反犹、被嘲讽“这也叫黑客”、对摄影过度敌视等，长期累积后降低归属感。  
• 部分评论担忧安全与管理，提到曾有抢劫未遂后安保人员处理不当，希望主办方改进；也有人认为不应对志愿运营组织抱有过高“服务消费者”式期待。  
• 许多人关心门票难抢、外地人参与难度及年底举办对有家庭或工作的人的限制；有人推荐规模较小的Datenspuren作为替代。  
• “Model Citizens”引发玩笑和解读：有人怀念早期更叛逆的氛围，也有人猜测与AI模型有关；另有观点将CCC视作对DEFCON右翼、厌女文化的乌托邦式反例。

补充讨论：评论还提议邀请Cliff Stoll或Markus Hess相关人物交流；整体争议焦点是CCC理想化的包容、自由文化，与现实中的社交摩擦、安保问题和组织门槛之间的落差。

49737787.article_content:
The word is on the street: the Chaos Computer Club is hosting 40C3 from 27 to 30 December 2026 – Europe’s biggest hacker party, conference and platform for technology, society and civil liberties. We understand the Congress to be a huge shared stage and therefore invite you to help shape it. The Call for Participation for talks, the entertainment programme, art, punk and music opens today.
Everything is getting bigger, more colourful and more beautiful. Following
our moving to the Hamburg Exhibition halls
, there is once again plenty of space for creative ideas. Obviously, we want to make the most of this new space, which is why we are inviting all galactic beings to the 40th Chaos Communication Congress from 27 to 30 December 2026.
With the idea of this year’s motto ‘Model Citizens’ in mind, we want to work together to find new models for society, now that the ‘Model Citizens’ of the past have left the planet in a precarious state. There are loads of ways to go about this. For example, the Congress is the biggest non-commercial hacker conference, organised by volunteers, supported by thousands of unpaid helpers and over 16,000 visitors who don’t just passively consume the event, but actively help to shape it.
Times have become harsher. The consensus that, in a democratic society, we should work in solidarity towards a shared, better future is increasingly giving way to the model of an authoritarian state, in which the stronger impose their views on the weaker. Personal commitment and a sense of responsibility are taking a back seat to the call for a strong hand that is supposed to make everything ‘great again’. The remaining liberal forces are fighting rearguard actions and no longer attempt to create something new, but merely to prevent things from getting worse.
We see things differently, with a more combative spirit: the Congress was and remains the model for how things can be different. Differences are seen as an asset, the unfamiliar as a source of inspiration, and mutual needs as an opportunity to create a sense of community in which everyone feels comfortable and welcome.
For our time-honoured lecture programme at 40C3, we are calling
for speakers to respond to our Call for Content
; we are also
reaching out to DJs and musicians to bring their talents to our lounge and party stages
. Artists and designers can
apply via our Call for Art
with exhibits, sculptures and performances that do not require a stage. For our Punk-Späti,
we’re looking for accomplices and fellow troublemakers
for anarchic and anti-fascist performances in our usual warm yet rough-and-ready atmosphere.

data.title: My temporary PHP fix from 2014 has nearly 20M installs. Today I'm deprecating it
data.author: jakeasmith
data.article_summary: 作者回顾了2014年为AOL CMS编写的174行PHP URL函数兼容补丁。该补丁原本只是临时方案，却通过Packagist安装近2000万次，并被多个项目和操作系统打包使用。由于长期无人维护且存在严重漏洞，作者决定将其弃用，建议用户迁移至PHP League URI库或PHP 8.5内置的标准URI API。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：一个使用广泛达12年的 PHP `http_build_url` polyfill 宣布弃用，引发对临时修复、开源依赖、遗留代码维护及安全风险的讨论。

不同观点：
• 作者认为，PHP及社区已有更好替代方案，经过12年后弃用是合适时机；但有人建议发布带迁移提示的最终版本，帮助用户从旧教程和依赖中迁移。  
• 有人批评原实现过于取巧：通过给路径追加“a”再截断，导致带尾斜杠时误删路径中所有“a”。评论者认为，简单功能应直接实现，避免让大量项目依赖临时方案。  
• 另一派强调 PHP 扩展生态和托管环境的限制，认为这些小型包是绕过服务器配置问题的实用补丁；也有人由此设想应从根本上设计更好的语言和基础设施。  
• 20M 次安装及 Hyrum 定律意味着，即使是 bug 也可能被用户依赖；有人担忧大量网站可能已受影响，也有人调侃它甚至可能被当作“删除字母 a”的功能。

补充讨论：评论分享了临时表长期成为业务依赖、个人包意外获得数百万安装等案例，说明临时修复容易固化为技术债。另有建议明确仓库是否归档，并关注被遗弃扩展在 AI 时代演变为安全风险的可能性。

Twelve years ago, I wrote

as a stopgap for AOLâs content management system. I put it on Packagist in case anyone else needed the same patch, and somehow itâs been installed nearly 20 million times since. Today I marked it deprecated.
A temporary shim
In 2014, we were in the middle of upgrading AOLâs CMS from PHP 5.2 to 5.3. Part of that upgrade was dropping version 1 of the
pecl_http
extension, which gave us a function called
http_build_url()
. A CMS deals with a lot of URLs, and ours called that function in dozens of places. I wasnât touching those. The function seemed straightforward enough to reproduce, so I wrote my own
http_build_url()
, defined only if the real one didnât already exist. The old code never knew anything had changed.
Composer was just taking off at the time, which made sharing it easy. I figured it would earn its keep for a year or two, until the PHP community moved on to something better.
Thatâs a lot of installs
Well, it wasnât temporary. Itâs been installed from Packagist nearly 20 million times, and it still picks up over 400,000 installs a month.
And it turns out Composer is only part of the picture.
WPML
, the market-leading multilingual plugin for WordPress, bundles the polyfill directly in its codebase, and WPML says itâs installed on over 1.5 million sites. The domain-name library
idna-convert
depends on it too, which is how it ships inside
the source of SPIP
, a French content management system, and how it ended up
packaged in Debian
and Ubuntu. Between all of them, thereâs a pretty good chance youâve visited a website that is still running my code.
I never imagined it would go this far.
Coming back to it
I didnât grasp how far it had spread until a few months ago, when I looked at the package for the first time in years. I knew it had users. By 2021 Iâd been out of PHP for a while, and the downloads were surprising enough that I
asked for a new maintainer
. Three people offered. Shortly after I asked, we lost a family member unexpectedly, and it turned our world upside down for a while. I never followed up, and thatâs on me. By the time things settled, other goals had taken over, and I forgot about the package for years.
Along with the numbers, there were a handful of GitHub issues, including one where joining a path onto a URL with a trailing slash strips every letter âaâ out of the path. So much for straightforward. Under a comment that reads
// Workaround for trailing slashes
, my code tacks an âaâ onto the path so thereâs always a last segment to cut off, then cuts it off with a find-and-replace. When the path ends in a slash, that last segment is just the âaâ, and the find-and-replace takes every other âaâ in the path with it. I canât believe the bug went unnoticed for as long as it did.
So I had a decision to make. I could dive back into PHP after almost a decade away, hand the package to one of the people whoâd offered, or let it keep sitting there.
None of the above
It was always meant to be temporary, so Iâm retiring it.
The PHP Leagueâs URI library
has been the communityâs answer for years, and
PHP 8.5
now ships
a standards-compliant URI API in the language itself
(thanks to
jawira
for pointing me at it). Both are better than a 174-line shim from 2014. Maintaining the package would only delay the move everyone should be making, and handing it over would add a risk on top of that. I donât doubt anyone who offered, and
ozh
has kept
a fork
going for YOURLS. But a widely installed package with a new maintainer nobody downstream has vetted is exactly what attackers look for.
Veritasiumâs video on the xz Utils backdoor
is the best telling Iâve seen of how that plays out.
The package will keep installing, but it wonât get new fixes, including for the missing-âaâ bug. After this long without a change, even a one-line fix could have unintended consequences for someone, with no one around to support it.
The README
shows how to switch.
I wrote this code to ease a painful migration, for myself and anyone else going through the same one. Thank you to everyone who sent a pull request or offered to take it over, and to the people who kept filing issues long after Iâd stopped reading them. It was a good run for a temporary fix.
P.S. We never migrated AOLâs CMS off the âtemporaryâ polyfill. It ran there until the whole platform was shut down around 2020.
49718773.article_summary: 作者回顾了2014年为AOL CMS编写的174行PHP URL函数兼容补丁。该补丁原本只是临时方案，却通过Packagist安装近2000万次，并被多个项目和操作系统打包使用。由于长期无人维护且存在严重漏洞，作者决定将其弃用，建议用户迁移至PHP League URI库或PHP 8.5内置的标准URI API。
49718773.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：一个使用广泛达12年的 PHP `http_build_url` polyfill 宣布弃用，引发对临时修复、开源依赖、遗留代码维护及安全风险的讨论。

不同观点：
• 作者认为，PHP及社区已有更好替代方案，经过12年后弃用是合适时机；但有人建议发布带迁移提示的最终版本，帮助用户从旧教程和依赖中迁移。  
• 有人批评原实现过于取巧：通过给路径追加“a”再截断，导致带尾斜杠时误删路径中所有“a”。评论者认为，简单功能应直接实现，避免让大量项目依赖临时方案。  
• 另一派强调 PHP 扩展生态和托管环境的限制，认为这些小型包是绕过服务器配置问题的实用补丁；也有人由此设想应从根本上设计更好的语言和基础设施。

data.title: Keys Not Included: recovering the signing keys for US driver's license barcodes
data.author: Ryan5453
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕驾驶证条码中的数字签名、公钥验证机制及其对伪造、数字身份和实际核验流程的影响展开讨论。

不同观点：
• **公开公钥并非安全问题**：有人认为公钥本来就应公开；后量子计算和国家级密钥收集虽构成长期威胁，但影响将远超身份验证领域。  
• **伪造条码的具体方式存在争议**：dmurray指出，ZNB字段并非空白或垃圾，而是格式正确但验签失败的ECDSA签名；他推测伪造者更可能复用了其他真实证件的签名，只替换了数据，而不是自行生成密钥。  
• **条码验证仍不足以证明持证人真实**：有观点认为照片也必须纳入并签名，否则收集少量真实证件即可覆盖发色、眼睛、肤色等特征；“假照片+有效条码”可能通过现有检查，除非配合额外的人脸或照片数据库。  
• **数字驾照前景乐观**：mDL及Apple Wallet等方案可让银行等机构在用户同意后获取证件信息，并逐步建立从州政府签发者到验证方的密码学信任链，可能优于物理证件；也有人称赞其无需依赖第三方应用。  
• **制度与用户体验问题**：评论询问邮寄新证时旧证如何处理；也有人指出现实中商店只扫描条码，假证即可带来便利，暴露出“可扫描”不等于“可信”。  
• **验证服务和教育仍欠缺**：州政府虽具备让公众验签的能力，却未必提供服务；应明确提醒验证者还要核对条码数据与证件可读文字，并用更准确的方式向非技术人员解释非对称密码学。

补充讨论：有人建议将类似签名机制用于纸币防伪；另有评论强调应归功于开源可验证凭证库，而非供应商。

data.title: Better Vector Search for Long Documents: Chunking Inside Manticore Search
data.author: GloriaVinogrado
data.article_summary: 文章介绍 Manticore Search 的文档分块向量检索功能：通过在向量列设置 `chunk_strategy`，自动将长文档切分、分别生成嵌入并检索，无需外部处理。支持 truncate、mean、fixed、recursive、sentence 五种策略及块大小、重叠和数量限制。搜索结果仍按文档返回，距离取最相关分块。实测召回率由55.1%提升至83.3%，但内存约增2.5倍、写入耗时约增4倍。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：文章中嵌入模型的输入长度限制，以及由此引发的分块、检索质量和用户体验问题。

不同观点：
• **批评512-token限制**：entrope认为512 token过短，会导致需要大量重叠分块；短文本上下文不足，且文档常有重复开头（如代码中的`#include <foo.h>`），容易造成截断和检索失真。文档被截断部分无法检索，系统也不提示用户，属于不友好的默认行为。  
• **长上下文并非根本解决方案**：hn45e7pbij指出，8K或更大的窗口虽然能减少截断，却不能消除分块需求。若把整段8K文本压缩为一个向量，多个主题会被“揉在一起”，同样可能降低检索质量。  
• **总体持积极态度**：Chance-Device认为该内容对自行搭建RAG系统的人会很有用。  
• **补充模型实例**：mistrial9指出BGE-M3支持8,192 token输入，说明较长上下文已被部分嵌入模型采用。

补充讨论：争议焦点在于默认采用短输入并自动截断是否合理，以及长上下文应如何与合理分块结合。entrope还批评相关表述更像在替开发者辩护，而非向用户透明说明限制。

49738766.article_content:
Better Vector Search for Long Documents: Chunking Inside Manticore Search
Author:
Dmitrii Kuzmenkov
Published: Sep 15, 2026 - 33 Min read
View as markdown
Say you are building search over your team's internal documentation — guides, runbooks, postmortems. You have a table with
auto embeddings
: you insert text, Manticore runs the model and fills the vector column for you. (If that is new to you, start with
vector search in Manticore
.) You load a 4,000-word document. The insert succeeds. The search works. Everything looks fine.
Except the model you picked has a 512-token input window, and that document is about 5,000 tokens long. The model read the first 380 words and threw away the other 3,600. Nothing in the document past that point can ever be retrieved, and nothing anywhere told you. The embedding may not represent the document as a whole either.
Until now, you would usually split the document into several pieces yourself, create embeddings for each one, and then work out how to combine the results if you wanted document search rather than chunk search. Manticore now handles this in the table definition: add
chunk_strategy
to the vector column in
CREATE TABLE
, and Manticore splits each document into chunks, embeds every chunk, and searches all of them:
DROP
TABLE
IF
EXISTS
docs;
CREATE
TABLE
docs (
title text,
content text,
chunks float_vector_array knn_type
=
'hnsw'
hnsw_similarity
=
'cosine'
model_name
=
'Xenova/all-MiniLM-L6-v2'
from
=
'title,content'
chunk_strategy
=
'sentence'
max_tokens
=
'256'
overlap_tokens
=
'32'
);
That is the whole feature. No ingest pipeline, no splitter library, no second table for chunks, no
GROUP BY
to fold chunk hits back into documents.
TL;DR
Five strategies
:
truncate
(the old default),
mean
,
fixed
,
recursive
,
sentence
. Set with
chunk_strategy
on a model-backed vector column.
truncate
and
mean
produce one vector per document and work on a
float_vector
column.
fixed
,
recursive
and
sentence
produce many, so they need a
float_vector_array
column.
A document is still one search result.
Chunks compete individually, and Manticore returns the document once, with
knn_dist()
reporting the distance to its closest chunk.
k
counts documents, not chunks.
Tuning knobs
:
max_tokens
(chunk size),
overlap_tokens
(shared tokens between neighbors),
max_chunks
(ceiling per document).
Measured on the Manticore manual
(189 pages, ~298k words): for content buried past the model's window, recall@5 went from
55.1% → 83.3%
and MRR from
0.44 → 0.70
, at ~2.5× the RAM and ~4× the ingest time.
Queries are never chunked.
A query is short enough to embed as a whole; only stored documents are split.
The problem, shown with a small example
Suppose you have four documents:
Backup and restore runbook
— about 700 words, roughly 900 tokens. Backup schedules, retention, restore drills, credentials, capacity planning. The
last
section explains how to rotate the TLS certificate used by the replication port.
Monitoring and alerting guide
— unrelated.
Getting started with the CLI
— unrelated.
TLS and certificates for the HTTP API
— a short page that is
entirely
about certificates, and never mentions rotation or replication.
You can create the table and add the documents using the commands below.
So, what we have is: one table, three vector columns with the same source text — one column per strategy. A single
INSERT
fills all three, so the comparison conditions are identical:
DROP
TABLE
IF
EXISTS
docs;
CREATE
TABLE
docs (
title text,
body text,
v_truncate float_vector       knn_type
=
'hnsw'
hnsw_similarity
=
'cosine'
model_name
=
'Xenova/all-MiniLM-L6-v2'
from
=
'title,body'
,
v_mean     float_vector       knn_type
=
'hnsw'
hnsw_similarity
=
'cosine'
model_name
=
'Xenova/all-MiniLM-L6-v2'
from
=
'title,body'
chunk_strategy
=
'mean'
,
v_sentence float_vector_array knn_type
=
'hnsw'
hnsw_similarity
=
'cosine'
model_name
=
'Xenova/all-MiniLM-L6-v2'
from
=
'title,body'
chunk_strategy
=
'sentence'
max_tokens
=
'128'
overlap_tokens
=
'32'
);
Insert the four documents
INSERT
INTO
docs (id, title, body)
VALUES
(
1
,
'Backup and restore runbook'
,
'Nightly backups run at 02:00 UTC from the standby node. The job snapshots every table directory, writes a manifest, and uploads the result to object storage. Retention is thirty daily copies, twelve monthly copies, and one yearly copy. A restore drill runs on the first Monday of each month against a scratch cluster. The drill counts as passed only when a full-text search over the restored data returns the same document count as production. Anything less is treated as a failed drill and investigated the same week. Before a restore, freeze the target cluster so that no writes land while files are being replaced. Copy the manifest first and verify its checksum. If the checksum does not match, stop: a partial restore is worse than no restore, because the cluster will start and silently serve half the corpus. After the files are in place, unfreeze and let replication catch

data.title: GLM Built Its Own Inference Infrastructure
data.author: whiteros_e
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕GLM-5.3的国产算力基础设施、软件优化能力及实际使用体验，评论者讨论了出口限制的影响、技术可信度和商业竞争力。

不同观点：
• **出口限制反而促进自主创新**：有人认为美国芯片禁令迫使中国AI产业“适者生存”，加速自研芯片和推理系统；也有人称赞其在超大规模国产加速器集群上的工程实践。  
• **对技术成果持肯定态度**：评论认为GLM团队通过激进的内存优化和自动化研究，在受限硬件条件下提升效率，体现了工业级工程能力；“100,000枚国产加速器”被视为重大成就。  
• **对“全国产化”保持怀疑**：有人追问这些加速器是否在芯片设计、制造、存储和光刻等环节都完全国产，认为不能仅凭宣传确认端到端自主。  
• **质疑实际性能与服务能力**：多位用户反馈GLM通过Z.ai访问速度很慢、额度限制严格，认为宣传中的优化效果与实际体验不符；也有人质疑其价格高于Claude后，竞争优势是否只是更大Token额度。  
• **软件工程争议**：有人质疑生产推理使用Python会带来臃肿、速度和全局锁问题；另一些评论则认为关键在整体系统优化，不能仅凭语言选择否定成果。  
• **美国也可复制该路径**：评论指出美国AI实验室投入巨大，却未必充分进行软件优化，若加强此方向可能缓解算力瓶颈。  
• **其他应用探索**：有人展示了用MacBook配合NVMe硬盘流式运行744B模型，虽速度有限但输出一致，说明低成本推理仍有探索空间。

补充讨论：部分评论以讽刺口吻质疑AI系统“不可靠”或所谓“意外能力”；讨论核心争议在于官方性能与用户体验的落差，以及国产化和优化成果的真实边界。

• **质疑实际性能与服务能力**：多位用户反馈GLM通过Z.ai访问速度很慢、额度限制严格，认为宣传中的优化效果与实际体验不符；也有人质疑其价格高于Claude后，竞争优势是否只是更大Token额度。  
• **软件工程争议**：有人质疑生产推理使用Python会带来臃肿、速度和全局锁问题；另一些评论则认为关键在整体系统优化，不能仅凭语言选择否定成果。  
• **美国也可复制该路径**：评论指出美国AI实验室投入巨大，却未必充分进行软件优化，若加强此方向可能缓解算力瓶颈。  
• **其他应用探索**：有人展示了用MacBook配合NVMe硬盘流式运行744B模型，虽速度有限但输出一致，说明低成本推理仍有探索空间。

补充讨论：部分评论以讽刺口吻质疑AI系统“不可靠”或所谓“意外能力”；讨论核心争议在于官方性能与用户体验的落差，以及国产化和优化成果的真实边界。

data.title: The Relation Between Mathematics and Physics by Paul Dirac (1939)
data.author: rramadass
data.article_summary: 狄拉克探讨数学与物理的深层关系。物理学依靠实验观察和数学推理，而自然界展现出适合数学描述的内在特性。经典力学强调基本定律的方程应简单；相对论则表明，数学美和结构深度比表面简单更重要。数学不仅描述自然，还能预言未进行的实验，未来物理学的发展将更加依赖抽象、优美的数学。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：数学为何能有效描述自然，以及数学结构是否只是物理语言，还是现实的基础。

不同观点：
• 数学—物理关系的乐观立场：自然规律往往呈现简单、优美的方程，奥卡姆剃刀可作为构建物理理论的原则；相关研究甚至尝试由简约性推出拉格朗日量和作用量原理。  
• 数学实在论/结构主义：数学规律可能反映自然的内在结构，甚至构成现实本身。评论提到狄拉克关于“变换”基础性的思想，以及以状态演化、组合和转换描述宇宙的 Functional Universe；也有人联系彭罗斯、玻姆的“隐缠序”。  
• 怀疑与经验主义：数学有效性未必意味着自然具有神秘的“数学品质”。观察规律只在特定时期和条件下成立，休谟式归纳问题提醒人们“有效直到失效”，不应把数学神圣化。  
• 数学与物理尚未完全匹配：数学家偏好的方向未必对应自然现象，如湍流、宏观量子现象、人择原理、有限主义等，二者的契合程度仍可进一步量化。  
• 宇宙与数学复杂性：有人引用狄拉克关于宇宙历史对应自然数序列的设想，并追问这是否预示了蔡廷不完备性；但该联系本身存在质疑。  
• 延伸观点：AI或能帮助发现新物理，关键在于让其提出有价值的问题。

补充讨论：评论还涉及狄拉克的宗教观及“狄拉克是上帝先知”的轶事，并有年份标注等编辑性意见。

(portrait by R. Tollast, 1963; reproduced by permission of the Master and Fellows of
St. John's College, Cambridge)
The Relation between Mathematics and
Physics
Paul Adrien Maurice Dirac
Lecture delivered  on presentation of the JAMES SCOTT prize, February 6,
1939
Published in: Proceedings of the Royal Society (Edinburgh) Vol. 59,
1938-39, Part II  pp. 122-129
The physicist, in his study of natural phenomena, has two methods of
making progress: (1) the method of experiment and observation, and (2)
the method of mathematical reasoning.  The former is just the collection
of selected data; the latter enables one to infer results about
experiments that have not been performed.  There is no logical reason
why the second method should be possible at all, but one has found in
practice that it does work and meets with reasonable success.  This must
be ascribed to some mathematical quality in Nature, a quality which the
casual observer of Nature would not suspect, but which nevertheless
plays an important role in Nature's scheme.
One might describe the mathematical quality in Nature by saying that the
universe is so constituted that mathematics is a useful took in its
description.  However, recent advances in physical science show that
this statement of the case is too trivial.  The connection between
mathematics and the description of the universe goes far deeper than
this, and one can get an appreciation of it only from a thorough
examination of the various facts that make it up.  The main aim of my
talk to you will be to give you such an appreciation.  I propose to deal
with how the physicist's views on this subject have been gradually
modified by the succession of recent developments in physics, and then I
would like to make a little speculation about the future.
Let us take as our starting-point that scheme of physical science which
was generally accepted in the last century - the mechanistic scheme.
This considers the whole universe to be a dynamical system (of course an
extremely complicated dynamical system), subject to laws of motion which
are essentially of the Newtonian type.  The role of mathematics in this
scheme is to represent the laws of motion by equations, and to obtain
solutions of the equations referring to observed conditions.
The dominating idea in this application of mathematics to physics is
that the equations representing the laws of motion should be of a simple
form.  The whole success of the scheme is due to the fact that equations
of simple form do seem to work.  The physicist is thus provided with a
principle of simplicity, which he can use as an instrument of research.
If he obtains, from some rough experiments, data which fit in roughly
with certain simple equations, he infers that if he performed the
experiments more accurately he would obtain data fitting in more
accurately with the equations.  The method is much restricted, however,
since the principle of simplicity applies only to fundamental laws of
motion, not to natural phenomena in general.  For example, rough
experiments about the relation between the pressure and volume of a gas
at a fixed temperature give results fitting in with a law of inverse
proportionality, but it would be wrong to infer that more accurate
experiments would confirm this law with greater accuracy, as one is here
dealing with a phenomenon which is not connected in any very direct way
with the fundamental laws of motion.
The discovery of the theory of relativity made it necessary to modify
the principle of simplicity.  Presumably one of the fundamental laws of
motion is the law of gravitation which, according to Newton, is
represented by a very  simple equation, but, according to Einstein,
needs the development of an elaborate technique before its equation can
even be written down.  It is true that, from the standpoint of higher
mathematics, one can give reasons in favour of the view that Einstein's
law of gravitation is actually simpler than Newton's, but this involves
assigning a rather subtle meaning to simplicity, which largely spoils
the practical value of the principle of simplicity as an instrument of
research into the foundations of physics.
What makes the theory of relativity so acceptable to physicists in spite
of its going against the principle of simplicity is its great
mathematical beauty.  This is a quality which cannot be defined, any
more than beauty in art can be defined, but which people who study
mathematics usually have no difficulty in appreciating.  The theory of
relativity introduced mathematical beauty to an unprecedented extent
into the description of Nature.  The restricted theory changed our ideas
of space and time in a way that may be summarised by stating that the
group of transformations to which the space-time continuum is subject
must be changed from the Galilean group to the Lorentz group.  The

data.title: Lucasart's Afterlife
data.author: Bondi_Blue
data.article_summary: 文章回顾Lucasarts经典游戏《Afterlife》，将其比作“天堂与地狱版《模拟城市》”，并分享重玩后的机制观察与攻略思路。作者讨论了关闭灾害、使用金钱秘籍、天堂与地狱的道路布局、区域及建筑“氛围”、邻接加成、建筑升级和人口变化等机制，并尝试总结天堂偏好多样化、地狱偏好单一化的分区策略。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕老牌 LucasArts 游戏的怀旧体验、设计特色、难度、流传现状及公司历史展开讨论。

不同观点：
• 怀旧与情感认同：多位评论者回忆童年玩《Afterlife》《Yoda Stories》等作品，认为当时游戏不依赖高分辨率、画面和帧率，创意、幽默、音乐与整体设计更重要；有人尤其怀念 LucasArts 的“黄金时代”。  
• 游戏特色与影响：评论者称赞《Afterlife》的美术、主题、配音和幽默；两位顾问角色令人印象深刻，游戏甚至较早让玩家体会到“债务”的危险。LucasArts 作品也影响了玩家对幽默和优秀配音的期待。  
• 难度评价不一：有人认为《Afterlife》小时候完全不会玩，成年后才想重新尝试；也有人觉得后期难度很高，但另一些玩家认为它很有趣，并未感到特别困难。  
• 作品被低估与后续缺失：有人认为该游戏理念创新但略显粗糙，若有续作本可完善机制、修正缺陷；评论者遗憾其没有续集，也几乎无人再关注。  
• 传播与获取困难：不少人想寻找正版或可运行版本，却发现游戏已极其罕见；有人则只见过广告、从未真正玩过，认为它不该因发行商知名而变得如此冷门。  
• 旁支讨论：有人澄清 LucasArts 原本就是游戏子公司，早期作品使用“Lucasfilm”品牌；另有人将文章主题误解为 LucasArts 被出售后的生活，或把讨论延伸到其他成人冒险游戏。

补充讨论：音乐、开场动画和教程也成为具体的怀旧记忆；评论整体偏正面，但核心争议集中在游戏究竟是“有趣的挑战”还是“过于困难”。

49719751.article_content:
Tags
Afterlife
I can hardly believe I’m writing a blog post about a game that came out 27 years ago, but here we are.    Lucasfilm, at one time had a gaming subsidiary called Lucasarts, and they produced something that has never been sequeled or surpassed : Afterlife.     Here is your elevator pitch for this game – “What if you combined Simcity with Heaven and Hell ?”
I clearly remember loving this game, playing up until 2 billion souls, and being so frustrated with certain aspects that I hex edited game files in an attempt to unlock the Omnibolges.  But I don’t have all the details.   After a fair amount of searching through the interwebs I have found only a few sources of information about the game.    This is also the only game with no subreddit dedicated to it.
Forum Posts from 2013
laying out bits of strategy.
The Afterlife FAQ
– this is vintage ’90s, when we put these massive text documents together.     And the really surprising thing, an
Article from November 2023
from a guy who clearly loves the game and “has beaten it”.
After starting and stopping a few different games, I have thoughts about tactics and game mechanics.    And I need notes to get to the point where I win as well.
BAD THINGS – Turn them off.    You get half the soul rate, but leaving them on guarantees both boredom watching the nose/picnic basket, and they ruin your super fiddly carefully constructed astral plane.
MONEY CHEAT – I highly doubt you can get through the game without at least one money cheat.    It’s $@! which I remember as SHIFT-421.    This is due to the strange negative cashflow you start out with and need to manage down by growing the size of your heaven/hell.
ROADS – Roads are odd in this game.    You want them to be inefficient in Hell which suggests one super long snaky road.     Yet I also remember reaching a point where the roads have a bug – no one is on them.   After they get a certain population there’s probably some overflow error.     In 2023 I have not reached that point.
An example of Hell Roads.    The gate on the left feeds a long snaky road on some astral real estate.
Roads in Heaven should be efficient, so think nice squares with zones / infrastructure in the middle.    For neither do I think I have the best building strategy yet.
Heavenly Road example.    Not perfect, I’ve found, but gets the idea across.
ZONES WITH VIBES
Each type of zone – or color – puts out a certain type of vibe.   To make matters worse, as you go through the development cycle, each zone goes from positive vibes to negative, or from negative to positive, or bounces from positive to negative ending in no vibes.  So far I’ve ignored this dynamic since you have incredibly limited ways to influence the vibes in the game.    And this may be a big problem.
INFRASTRUCTURE WITH VIBES
Some buildings put out positive vibes, like the Topias, Training Centers, and Reward buildings.    Others put out negative like Gates, Karma Trains, Siphons, and Karma Portals.
ADJACENCY BONUSES
Heaven likes to be diverse.    You’d like each zone to have as many different other types next to it as possible.     Of course Hell is the opposite – a sea of Green gives the best adjacency bonus.
SIZE SURPRISES
Several buildings go through an upgrade cycle.   At least one will screw you up.     Your first gate will probably be 3×3, and so will the second.    The third gate is a 4×4 building.    It will spill over when upgraded if room is available, and if not you can’t build it.     There may be others.
POPULATION SURPRISE
When you first sit down and look at the game you’d think “I get it.   Those 1×1 buildings have certain population sizes, and better ones have more size”.    This is true – but the size amount changes as the game progresses.    In other words, the population in any specific 1×1 building gets larger as time goes on.  This deserves some documentation.    Later.
ZONING STRATEGY – HEAVEN
The obvious strategy would be to go for 3×3 buildings in some kind of road box.    Pearson recommends 2×2, which I haven’t tried out yet.    I’ve had good success getting 3×3 buildings so I think the next game includes 3×3 as a goal.
This might be called “3×3 Heaven Doubles”.   Looks good.
“3×3 Heaven Triples” like this, doesn’t work well.     You could put some kind of non-road-building in the center but these don’t exist.    You only get five reward buildings and these are 4×4.
It is possible that if you modified the above to fit 4×4 buildings, that would be a good strategy.   You could introduce more diversity for the corners that way.    The center zones get 4 diversity which is probably the maximum.
All this said, I feel pretty good about the first idea for Heaven.
ZONING STRATEGY – HELL
Assuming a goal of 3×3 buildings, you want as little diversity as possible.    Only roads and the same type of zone next to each other.     The trick is, the 3×3 buildings never seem to develop if you make a gigantic zone, just look at that first screenshot.    25 million souls

data.title: Show HN: Share your AI Setup, Learn from others
data.author: steveybrown
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了一个分享个人 AI 工作流与工具配置的社区网站。作者因对各种 AI 工具、代理框架、技能和工程方法感到困惑，创建该平台，让工程师、创作者和开发者展示并比较自己的 AI setup，交流经验、发现新工具，也便于持续更新和分享个人配置。文章还展示了几位用户的 AI 开发工作流。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕一个通过 MCP/GitHub 自动读取并分享个人 AI 工作流的平台，评论集中在安全隐私、参与门槛、信息价值与实际使用成本。

不同观点：
• 安全与隐私担忧：vegadw、selicos、river_otter 不愿连接陌生 MCP、GitHub 账号或本地工具，担心凭证、配置和项目数据泄露，要求支持直接提交 Markdown；这成为最集中争议。
• 对分享意愿的质疑：hackmack10 认为 AI 工作流已是生产力和职业竞争力，不应公开；但 fenaer、realjohng 等希望看到真实的本地部署、热门方案和新手推荐。
• 产品功能建议：thoughtpeddler 希望支持按工具搜索，而非仅按用户浏览；realjohng 建议统计并展示热门配置；OtherShrezzing 要求显示月度成本，因部分方案每月超过400美元。
• “看源码/提示词”更有价值：shrikant 认为直接查看提示词比使用小工具更实用，并改写为“先生成私密草稿、预览、明确批准后发布”，强调最小权限和人工确认。
• 使用方式差异：有人仅用 Claude/Codex、EC2、tmux；有人依赖本地模型和基础设施。nowittyusername 分享了 OpenAI 模型、低延迟语音输入、自定义上下文压缩等复杂工作流。

补充讨论：成本也是焦点，sanex 质疑 Claude API 价格；评论整体反映出“自动发现越深入，隐私风险越高”的矛盾。

security-audit
A coding-agent skill that turns your agent into a security auditor. It orchestrates isolated agents through reconnaissance, coverage-led hunting, candidate validation, structured output, independent record verification, and target-neutral reporting.
This is the skill that seeded Cloudflare's vulnerability discovery harness, described in
Build your own vulnerability harness
. The harness grew into a multi-stage, fleet-wide system; this skill is the single-repo starting point it evolved from.
What it does
The skill runs a structured audit in six phases:
Reconnaissance
-- map architecture, trust boundaries, input surfaces, prior evidence, and deterministic coverage in
architecture.md
and
coverage-ledger.json
.
Coverage-led hunting
-- assign isolated hunters from ledger units, record their checks, and use coverage critics to find gaps.
Candidate validation
-- give every unique candidate to a fresh verifier that tries to disprove it.
Structured output
-- write
confirmed
,
needs_validation
, and
rejected
records to
findings.json
and validate them against
report-schema.json
.
Independent record verification
-- fresh agents verify final source claims. Material replacements receive another independent verifier.
Target-neutral reporting
-- derive
REPORT.md
,
FINDINGS-DETAIL.md
, and
NEEDS-VALIDATION.md
from the verified records and coverage ledger.
The parent runs
validate-coverage-ledger.cjs
after creating the ledger and after each later ledger update. It runs
validate-findings.cjs
in Phase 4 and again after every Phase 5 replacement.
The verdicts are distinct:
confirmed
has a complete source trace and bounded observed result,
needs_validation
has an exact unresolved fact and no severity, and
rejected
records a disproved candidate.
Multiple runs against the same repo are additive. The skill uses prior ledgers and findings to target gaps, revalidate changed source, and carry forward current-source evidence without treating stale or unresolved work as covered.

data.title: Comparison of Malloc() Algorithms
data.author: egberts1
data.article_summary: 文章介绍多线程内存分配的性能瓶颈：频繁调用传统malloc会因全局锁和堆竞争导致扩展性下降，尤其不应在每个数据包到达时分配内存。文章回顾了内存分配器前后端、线程缓存、Arena、NUMA及无锁结构的演进，并比较jemalloc、tcmalloc、mimalloc、snmalloc等方案，指出采用线程/CPU本地缓存、多Arena和低原子操作设计可提升并发性能、降低碎片与竞争。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：文章内容与其特殊 SSL 配置引发的可访问性、技术准确性及内存分配器历史讨论。

不同观点：
• SSL 配置是刻意设计的展示：作者通过仅支持 ChaCha/Poly 的协商方式，展示某些浏览器拒绝该方案的原因；但评论者推测 Chromium、Windows Firefox、curl 及手机浏览器均无法连接，质疑其可用性。  
• 多人认为应优先提供“如何配置 SSL”的说明，认为当前设置造成了不必要的访问障碍。  
• 有评论批评文章技术表述不严谨：把分配器并发串行化、处理器越多性能越差作为开头论点，即使后文撤回，也会误导读者；此外将 arena 归因于 2006 年 jemalloc、声称其为 jemalloc 术语，忽略了更早的相关思想和术语来源。还指出“CPU infinity”应为“CPU affinity”。  
• 另一位评论者虽无法访问文章，但分享了 1990 年代早期的“buddy malloc”及其变体“donner malloc”故事：后者将伙伴块进一步切分成不同大小，名称取自“拆分伙伴”的双关，作为历史性实例补充主题。

补充讨论：争议核心一方面是特殊 SSL 配置究竟是有意的浏览器兼容性实验还是糟糕的部署；另一方面是文章在内存分配器并发性能、arena 历史及术语使用上的准确性。

49715318.article_content:
Memory Allocation
Problems
Limit Memory Allocation (if not necessary)
Multithreaded programs often do not scale because the heap is a
bottleneck.
When multiple threads simultaneously allocate or deallocate memory from
the allocator, the allocator will serialize them. Programs making
intensive use of the allocator actually slow down as the number of
processors increases.
Malloc (libc) is the worst memory allocation API to use.
Programs should avoid, if possible, allocating/deallocating memory too
often and in particular whenever a packet is received.
In the Linux kernel there are available kernel/driver patches for
recycling skbuff (kernel memory used to store incoming/outgoing
packets).
Using PF_RING (into the driver) for copying packets from the NIC to the
circular buffer without any memory allocation increases the capture
performance (around 10%) and reduces congestion issues.
Design Evolution
Basic design of malloc() is to dynamically pre-allocate a pool of memory
from the OS in which applications can then take smaller pieces from.
malloc() is a standard API having a choice of different allocation
algorithms and to mitigate the expensive OS system calls (typically done
at program initialization time) during allocation of its system memory.
The first memory allocation scheme started with a stack-based memory
allocation.
Next came the dynamic-based memory allocation scheme where linked-list
and bucket-heap mechanism are used to divide the private-heap using size
class approach.
Soon, garbage collection algorithm introduced the initial backend of the
memory allocation scheme. Frontend covers the usual
malloc()
API, et
al.
In 2006, a third pool was introduced (after operating system memory pool
and library-based memory pool) called the “arena”. Arena is a
jemalloc-term and is intended to deal with different memory types such
as different-speed memory bank or NUMA-architecture, as well as memory
tied to specific to each of the multiple CPU core or even CPU infinity.
Frontend Evolution
Frontend manages the memory being given to the application.
Within the frontend of the memory allocation system, the evolution went
in the following order:
link-list free space
heap-bucket size classes (eliminating an object header)
(Process) Owner encoding
single core local allocation buffers (CLABs)
Epoch encoding
Large-size class memory block by direct mmap()
Hazard pointers (safe memory reclamation for lock-free objects) (M.M. Michael, 2004)
Arena memory pool (CPU/core and thread, separately)
thread-specific local allocation buffers (TLABs)
constant-time modulo synchronization (early return to OS pool, or FreeBSD madvise call)
Backend Evolution
Backend of the memory allocation system manages the empty, straggling,
fragmented or no-longer used memory blocks back to the OS (thereby
reducing RSS).
Pool semantic: Remote f-list encoding, using Treiber stack), (R.K.  Treiber,  1986)
buddy algorithm
binary buddy algorithm
BIPOP Table (span-based allocator)(S. Schneider, 2006) aka local free list and remote free list
segment queue (Quasi-linearizability, Y. Afek, 2010)
multi-core distributed queue (A. Haas, 2013)
k-FIFO queue (T.A. Henzinger, 2013)
Competition
There are better ones out there that does not worsen as more threads/processes performs memory allocation system calls; they are listed in best-to-good performance order [seed with source]:

data.title: Developing provably correct Rust code with Verus
data.author: Betelbuddy
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了开源自动程序验证器Verus。它允许开发者在Rust代码中直接编写数学规格、前置条件和后置条件，并自动证明代码对所有输入均符合预期，弥补传统测试遗漏边界情况的不足。Verus还能验证unsafe代码和并发程序，支持AI辅助生成证明。亚马逊已将其用于Nitro隔离引擎等关键基础设施，相关技术也被证书验证、数据解析和分布式系统等开源项目采用。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕 Verus（Rust 形式化验证工具）的能力、应用价值、可信边界及其与相关工具的比较展开讨论。

不同观点：
• **积极认可**：认为 Verus 可为 API、重构和性能优化提供确定性的机器检查，尤其结合 LLM，可能提升代码正确率；有人称其“意义重大”，并计划认真尝试。  
• **工具生态与定位比较**：评论提到 Miri、Kani、Creusot、Whiley、Lean/Aeneas 等类似项目，认为 Verus、Kani、Creusot 存在功能重叠；另有人比较 Verus 与 TLA+，指出 TLA+偏向分布式系统设计和蓝图验证，而 Verus 能与 Rust 代码编译、集成。

Automated reasoning
Developing provably correct Rust code with Verus
How the Verus "program verifier", which automatically checks code against a mathematical specification of its functionality, helps increase security assurance in software projects.

Key takeaways
Verus is an open-source automated program verifier for Rust that mechanically checks code against formal mathematical specifications for all possible inputs, going beyond traditional testing to catch corner cases.
Developers annotate Rust source code directly with preconditions and postconditions using Rust-like syntax, enabling fast feedback loops (under one second) and allowing AI agents to assist in proof generation.
Verus enables mathematical verification of Rust's "unsafe" code blocks and concurrent code with custom locking schemes, re-establishing machine-checked safety guarantees for performance-critical implementations like AWS's Nitro Isolation Engine.
Amazon uses Verus to prove correctness of key primitives in critical infrastructure, and the tool has been adopted by open-source projects including certificate validation libraries, data format parsers, and distributed systems like Kubernetes controllers.
Was this answer helpful?
Many open-source and industry software projects, including
several
here
at Amazon
, are embracing the Rust programming language, since it provides performance and flexibility similar to that of the C programming language, while its clever type system automatically prevents a variety of bugs and security vulnerabilities. The result is fast code that's more correct and secure than average.
However, "more correct and secure" is not the same as "actually correct and secure". For example, in C, accessing an array out of bounds — indexing into an array past the boundary of the memory allotted to it — is a dangerous mistake that can have unforeseeable consequences. In Rust, it will halt the program, which is definitely safer, but a correct program would never perform the out-of-bounds access in the first place. Similarly, Rust cannot guarantee that your program will compute the results you were expecting or that it won't leak the secrets it has access to. That's where Verus comes in.
Accessing an array out of bounds is a dangerous mistake that can have unforeseeable consequences. A correct program would not permit it.
What is Verus?
Verus
is an open-source, automated program verifier for Rust. A "program verifier" takes in a formal mathematical specification of how your code should behave and mechanically checks that your code matches that specification for all possible inputs.
For example, your code might implement an optimized binary-search algorithm to look for a particular value within a sorted array. The specification might state that when the code successfully returns an index, the corresponding element in the array matches the target value. The verifier checks that this specification holds for all possible input arrays and target values.
In contrast, traditional testing techniques might try a few specific arrays but can miss corner cases (e.g., what if the target value is the last element in the array or not present at all?). A key aspect of program verification involves constructing a mathematical
proof
that the code matches its specification. In an
automated
program verifier like Verus, the tool automatically handles many of the boring, low-level steps of proof construction, while the human developer provides high-level guidance (e.g., setting up an inductive proof or supplying a loop invariant). As we discuss below, these days, even the high-level steps can often be automated by AI.
At Amazon, we're proud to have been a founding member of the Rust Foundation, and we use Rust extensively for projects like
Firecracker
, which powers AWS Lambda and AWS Fargate, our serverless distributed SQL database, and the
Nitro Isolation Engine
, which enforces virtual-machine isolation for the Nitro hypervisor, the software that manages virtual-machine allocation for Amazon Web Services (AWS). Amazon's excitement about Rust, combined with more than a
decade of work on automated reasoning
, makes it natural to adopt Verus to provide even stronger guarantees for the Rust code we're writing. Indeed, we've used Verus to prove the correctness of key primitives used by the Nitro Isolation Engine, as well as a number of critical pieces of infrastructure used within Amazon. We'll explore these use cases in future posts, but for now, we want to tell you more about what it means to verify Rust code with Verus.
Verifying Rust code with Verus

Iran school bombing: grounds to believe US was behind atrocity, UN finds
Fact-finding mission says military strikes on school and sports facility in ⁠February constitute war ⁠crimes
Peter Beaumont
and agencies
Thu 17 Sep 2026 09.22 EDT
First published on Thu 17 Sep 2026 05.05 EDT
Share
Prefer the Guardian on Google
A UN fact-finding mission has determined there are reasonable grounds to believe the US was behind military strikes on a school and a sports facility in
Iran
in ⁠February that killed 120 children, and that these constituted war ⁠crimes.
The school strike, which killed 156 civilians including 120 children, involved a US Tomahawk missile that collapsed the roof of the Shajareh Tayyebeh
primary school, which the UN said was “clearly identifiable”, in Minab, Hormozgan province, on 28 February.
The Pentagon’s own secretive investigation into the incident is understood to have concluded several months ago. There have been reports that senior US commanders had been warned that targeting data used during the war – including for the Minab strike – was dangerously outdated.
The second cited strike, on the same date, targeted a “clearly identifiable sports complex and residential area” in the southern city of Lamerd with a weapon that scattered tungsten pellets.
The UN fact-finding team said in a statement: “Following the United States and Israeli attacks on 28 February, the mission found reasonable grounds to believe the United States committed the war crime of launching indiscriminate attacks resulting in the loss of life or injury to civilians or damage to civilian objects.”
The mission also found Iranian ​authorities had committed crimes against humanity during their deadly crackdown on anti-government protests.
The findings by the independent international fact-finding mission on Iran, to be submitted to the UN human rights council in Geneva, examined the ⁠US’s conduct during the Iran war that began in February and the Iranian government’s response to
nationwide unrest that began in late December
.
US officials have previously said military ⁠operations are conducted in accordance with the law of armed conflict, while Iran has consistently rejected allegations of systematic rights violations.
The UN mission concluded that the strike on Shajareh Tayyebeh primary school constituted an indiscriminate attack causing civilian deaths and damage to ‌civilian infrastructure, amounting to a war crime under international law.
View image in fullscreen
A rubble-strewn classroom at Shajareh Tayyebeh school.
Photograph: Vahid Salemi/AP
According to the report, the US relied on intelligence suggesting a senior Iranian military commander was present at the site but failed to adequately verify the information before launching the strike.
Investigators said the failure to update targeting intelligence and confirm the building was a military objective amounted to more than mere negligence.
“Rather, the US directed the strikes at the building of the school while being aware of a substantial risk of striking a civilian object and acting recklessly as regards the possibility that this would happen.”
In June the US president, Donald Trump, said ‌“nobody” had purposely attacked a girls’ school in Iran in February, citing an investigation into the incident. The Pentagon has since elevated ​the inquiry, but it has not published any preliminary findings.
Four months after the horrific Iran school bombing, fears grow that Trump and Hegseth will bury the truth
Read more
UN experts said the school was a clearly identifiable civilian object and found no evidence it was being used for military purposes.
The experts reached a similar conclusion over the strike on the sports centre in Lamerd. The report said the attack had damaged nearby residential buildings and a school and killed and injured 22 civilians. It concluded that the strike had been indiscriminate and therefore constituted a war crime.
US Central Command said in a statement in March that ⁠US forces had not launched any strikes into the city of Lamerd on that day.
The UN mission also found ​that the Iranian authorities had carried out a widespread and systematic ​attack against civilians during
protests that erupted
in late ​December last year, involving unlawful killings, torture, arbitrary detention, enforced disappearances and severe restrictions on freedom of expression.
Rights groups say bystanders were among ​those killed during the biggest crackdown ‌since Shia Muslim clerics took ​power in the 1979 revolution. Tehran blamed “terrorists ​and rioters” backed by exiled opponents and the US and Israel.

补充讨论：两条评论并无直接争议，关系上是“应用评价”与“概念解释”的互补；潜在焦点在于如何通过更贴近真实问题的案例和文档，展示 Z3 的实际能力。

data.author: vertigoruntime
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：法律领域引入大模型的实际价值、能力边界及其对律师行业和司法系统的影响。

不同观点：
• **辅助增效而非替代律师**：大模型适合从多格式医疗/福利法律文件中提取信息、生成JSON，能将处理效率从每小时2–3份提升至8–10份，但仍需律师审核，不能承担法律判断。  
• **不同法律领域影响差异很大**：高价值人身伤害案件的核心成本在庭审辅助和诉讼策略，短期不太可能被AI或DIY取代；合同、专利、法律检索等标准化工作则更容易受影响。  
• **可靠性仍不足**：AI可能加入不现实或相互冲突的保护条款，误引已被推翻的判例，甚至产生幻觉；不具备理解和验证能力的用户使用AI，容易形成“看起来合理”的法律文本。  
• **性能评价存在争议**：Astra for Law在Vals基准上略低于Claude、Muse；严格准确率约54%，说明即便大部分内容正确，也可能因关键遗漏而失效。  
• **行业商业模式将被重塑**：OpenAI与律所合作可能把律所经验产品化，削弱品牌溢价；也有人质疑大厂战略分散，应用层可能被更专注的AI公司占据。  
• **潜在新风险与用途**：AI可能造成诉讼数量激增、法律“垃圾文本”泛滥，也可能被用于模拟法官偏好、设计针对性诉讼策略。

补充讨论：争议焦点在于AI究竟是律师的生产力工具，还是会侵蚀律师专业价值；评论还涉及判例“陷阱”、法律AI营销宣传及疑似AI灌水内容。
